title: Rance Halifax Memorial
memorial_details: Memorial sculpture near the village of Rance, Hainaut, remembering three local wartime crashes. Two are Bomber Command losses.
narrative:
The memorial at Rance, Hainaut, commemorates two 51 Squadron and 431 (RCAF) Squadron Halifax losses as well as a third (non-Bomber Command) crash.

Halifax JD262 of 51 Squadron, coded MH-E, departed Snaith at 2327 on 3 July 1943 for Cologne. It was shot down at 0240 by Oberleutnant Ludwig Meister of Stab I/NJG4, his 11th claim. Five crew were killed; one became a prisoner of war; one evaded.

Halifax LK884 of 431 (RCAF) Squadron, coded SE-X, departed Croft at 0107 on 9 May 1944 for Haine-Saint-Pierre. It was intercepted at 3000m in the Charleroi–Nivelles area by Unteroffizier Konrad Beyer of 1/NJG1 and shot down at 0331, his fourth claim. All seven crew were killed.

aircraft.cause_of_loss: Shot down by night fighter — Oblt Ludwig Meister (Stab I/NJG4), his 11th claim
Shot down by night fighter — Uffz Konrad Beyer (1/NJG1), his 4th claim
